summary: Dhammanandā specializes in Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~2003–2007) under Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe, also studying under Viên Minh, Toshiichi Endo, and Nicholas Armstrong Jayawickrama.

Dhammapāla works in Buddhist studies. He studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (until 2003) and earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (~2005–2009) under K. L. Dhammajoti, later serving there as 客座助理教授.

Dhirendra Mohan Datta was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1924). He held posts at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He studied under David Friedman (~1958–1961) and traditional teacher Surendra Sharma.

Dhivan Thomas Jones works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He has served as an associate lecturer at the Open University and held a post at the University of Chester in 2019.

Di Luo specializes in Sinology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Supervised by James Steele for an MA, Di Luo completed a PhD at the University of Southern California (~2010–2016) under Dominic Cheung, Sonya S. Lee, and Bettine Birge.

Diana L. Eck is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College (~1963–1967), SOAS (~1967–1968), and Harvard (~1970–1976). She became a professor at Harvard University around 1976.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. She held appointments as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane E. Riggs studied Japanology and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD at UCLA (~2002–2010) under William M. Bodiford. She held posts at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University.
Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed graduate studies at McMaster University under Graeme MacQueen, finishing in 1982.
Dickwela Piyananda specialized in Buddhist studies, completing a PhD at the Catholic University of America in 1974 under doctoral supervisor Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Cosmelli completed a PhD at École Polytechnique (~2000–2004), where he was supervised by Francisco Varela from ~2000 to 2001.
Diego Loukota specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned an MA from Peking University (~2013) and a PhD from UCLA (~2013–2019).

Dieter B. Kapp worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Direktor des Instituts für Indologie und Tamilistik at the University of Cologne (~1988–2006) and founded Beitrage zur Kenntnis sudasiatischer Sprachen und Literaturen.
Dieter George was an Indology scholar who held a post at the Berlin State Library from around 1972 to 1985, succeeding Wolfgang Voigt.
Dieter Maue works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He completed a doctoral dissertation at the University of Giessen in 1976 and later held a post there.

Dieter Schlingloff, an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology scholar, studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (until ~1952). He held posts at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (-1968), University of Kiel (~1968–1972), and University of Munich (~1972–1996).
Dieter Schrapel specialized in Indology. He completed his doctoral degree in 1970 at the University of Marburg under the supervision of Wilhelm Rau.

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Cologne in 1963 and under Klaus Ludwig Janert (~1967–1972). He served as special professor in Tibetology at the University of Bonn (~1978–2007).

Dietmar Rothermund was a historian and Indologist who studied at Munich (~1953–1954), Marburg (~1954–1956), and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD ~1956–1959). He held a post at Heidelberg University (~1968–1998).
